slides.heading: Building a Formatted Output
slides.body: Building a Formatted Output is part of Mathematical and String Operations. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Building a Formatted Output
slides.body: Formatted output arranges text and values clearly. It helps users understand results, receipts, and short reports.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Formatted output is like designing a clean menu board where each item and price is easy to read.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Use an f-string to show an item and its price in one line.

quiz.prompt_text: What does an f-string (formatted string) allow you to do in Python?

options: Convert a number to a boolean
Embed variable values directly inside a string using curly braces {}

quiz.explanation: Excellent! An f-string lets you insert variable values directly into text using {} placeholders. For example, f"{item}: {price} pesos" combines text and values neatly.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines in the correct order to format and print a store item with its price.
quiz.explanation: Both variables must be assigned before the f-string can reference them. The f-string then combines them into a formatted output in one clean line.

quiz.prompt_text: Use an f-string to print an item name and its price on one line in the format: Notebook: 35 pesos
quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: print(f"{item}: {price} pesos") inserts the values of item and price directly into the string. f-strings start with f before the opening quote.
